messages:
vikram: Quick flag — noticed a p99 regression for mistral-8x7b after the kernel-chooser tweak, mostly on sliding-window workloads. p50 unchanged but p95/p99 jumped ~1.6x. Repro on canary.
amy: Ugh. Which commit/PR? can you paste numbers and an example request?
vikram: Commit 3f9b2d9 (kernel-chooser: prefer lowest-expected-flops). Example traffic: long chat history with rolling window, seq_len ~1500 -> new tokens 256. p99 token latency went from ~42ms -> ~68ms.
vikram: Quick profiler snippet (GPU kernel times, trimmed):
```
model=mistral-8x7b seq=1500
kernel: sliding_window_v2            avg=9.2ms   p99=12.1ms
kernel: kv_copy                      avg=18.7ms  p99=26.3ms
kernel: rope_rescale                 avg=3.1ms   p99=4.5ms
overall token gen                     avg=45ms    p99=68ms
```
vikram: Looks like kernelselector picked kv_copy + separate rope_rescale instead of a combined sliding-window kernel that does RoPE inline. That extra copy + separate rescale explains the cliff.
jordan: We changed the score to use theoretical FLOPs based on matrix sizes; we didn't model the amortized cost of the sliding-window kernel which avoids copies + reuses KV. So for these mid-long sequences it picks the wrong path.
lucy: Also saw an attention-mask quirk: when rope_scale != 1.0 and max_pos_embeddings > runtime_window we forgot to shift the sliding-window offsets — rotations get applied with the wrong absolute positions. That causes small correctness drift + extra rescale ops.
amy: Do you have a small repro curl for bench-bot? want to run a microbenchmark across seq lengths.
vikram: Yep. Repro:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"mistral-8x7b","input":"<long chat>","max_new_tokens":256,"runtime_overrides":{"kernel_selector":"auto","rope_scale":1.0}}'
```
vikram: If you set runtime_overrides.kernel_selector=sliding_window_v2 the p99 drops back to ~44ms.
bench-bot: Automated run across seq lens (baseline vs post-chooser):
```
seq 512:  baseline 40ms  -> 42ms
seq 1024: baseline 41ms  -> 45ms
seq 1500: baseline 44ms  -> 68ms  <-- big
seq 2048: baseline 50ms  -> 82ms
```
bench-bot: Breakdown shows extra memory copy + rope_rescale kernel dominating when kernelselector chooses the non-sliding path.
jordan: That explains it. The heuristic underestimated the benefit of cache reuse and logical memory layout for sliding-window. We need to include estimated memcpy cost and rope rescale overhead in the cost model, plus a penalty if rope_scale != 1.0.
lucy: There's also the max_position_embeddings mismatch to handle: model metadata says mpe=8192 but runtime table was capped at 2048 for some of our deployments. When the table wraps the sliding offsets are wrong. Two bugs: (1) selection heuristic, (2) offset math when runtime_mpe < model_mpe and rope_scale != 1.0.
amy: Proposed mitigation?
vikram: Short term: patch kernelselector to prefer sliding_window_v2 for model==mistral-8x7b when seq_len > 1024 OR add a safety rule that if estimated memcpy+rescale > X prefer sliding. Also add a quick runtime flag to force kernel override per-deployment. Rolling a canary with that now.
jordan: Mid-term: update kernelselector cost model to account for memcpy + header/rescale kernels and add rope_scale multiplier; unit tests for sequence-length thresholds per-model.
lucy: I'll open a separate PR to fix the sliding-window offset math: when we apply RoPE scaling we must compute rotation indices using absolute position = base_pos + window_offset, not just window index. Also ensure we honor model.max_position_embeddings before truncating.
ops: Rolling canary with kernelselector patch to 5% tenant traffic now. Will watch p99.
deploy-bot: Canary started: 5% traffic -> hosts rtx-a[12-15].
vikram: Canary numbers after 10min: p99 back to ~46ms on canary, others still high. Looks promising.
amy: Ok rollback plan if needed?
ops: Auto-rollback if p99 increases >10% over baseline for 3 consecutive minutes. Alerting on.
vikram: Follow-ups:
- Jordan: cost-model PR to include memcpy/rescale and rope_scale penalty.
- Lucy: offset/rope scaling correctness + test vectors (wrap-around cases).
- Amy/Bench: run full sweep across seqs 256..4096 and produce a perf matrix.
- Infra: expose kernel override in runtime flags for urgent fixes.
vikram: Thanks all. Filing a short postmortem once we land fixes. :thumbsup:
